findings.description: KEY NORMALIZATION (trim + upper-case) — the headline gap, surfaced from both sides with opposite answers. CODE: `resolve_ticker(aliases, symbol)` in crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs:254-257 computes `let normalized = symbol.trim().to_uppercase(); aliases.resolve(&normalized)`. tests/mapping.rs:65-77 pins it hard: `resolve_ticker(&aliases,"brk")=="BRK.B"`, `"  BRK  "`→`"BRK.B"`, `" brk"`→`"BRK.B"`, and — critically — the identity path is normalized too: `resolve_ticker(&aliases," amzn ")=="AMZN"`. SPEC: SHEET-MAP-001 says only "via `config`'s alias map (identity when unset)" — no normalization rule anywhere, and the plain reading of "identity" is the ledger `Symbol` returned unchanged. B-SIDE: all 3 reconstructions promote normalization to a first-class clause (B1 SHEET-TICK-002/003, B2 001/003, B3 002/004) and all 3 explicitly state the fallback is the normalized form, not the raw input. A-SIDE: all 3 sketches implement the exact opposite and flag it as a forced invention — A1 assumption 3 "Lookup is exact/case-sensitive; no normalization, trimming, or uppercasing", A2 assumption 1 plus a test named `alias_map_is_case_sensitive_exact_match`, A3 assumption 4 "exact-match, case-sensitive. The EARS gives no normalization rule". CONSEQUENCE THE SPEC LICENSES NOBODY TO KNOW: because `config::AliasMap` (crates/config/src/lib.rs:277-300) stores keys verbatim (no normalization at `new`/`put_aliases`) and `resolve` is an exact `BTreeMap::get`, any alias entry whose key is not already upper-case/untrimmed — e.g. a user-typed `brk → BRK.B` on the Platforms & Aliases tab — is structurally unreachable and silently degrades to an identity ticker. Second consequence: with no alias configured at all, the emitted ticker can still differ from the ledger `Symbol` (` amzn ` → `AMZN`), which the spec's word "identity" forbids on its face.

THE RESOLVED TICKER DRIVES A SECOND, WHOLLY UNSTATED GOOGLEFINANCE FORMULA. SPEC: "...and build the `Price` formula from the resolved ticker" — one formula, named Price. CODE: `quote_date_formula(ticker)` (crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs:277-281) emits `=IFERROR(TEXT(INT(GOOGLEFINANCE("{ticker}","tradetime"))-DATE(1970,1,1),"0"),"")` and `render_positions` (line 597) builds it from the SAME resolved ticker as the Price cell, at `POSITIONS_HEADER` index 12 ("Quote Date"). tests/formula.rs:204-271 pins the whole encoding contract: `assert_eq!(qcol, 12)`, and per row the text must contain `GOOGLEFINANCE`, `tradetime`, `DATE(1970,1,1)`, `TEXT(`, `IFERROR`; plus "quote date rides the resolved ticker" — with alias `AMZN → NASDAQ:AMZN`, the Quote Date cell must contain `NASDAQ:AMZN`. Every load-bearing constant here (the `tradetime` attribute, the 1970-01-01 kernel Date epoch re-base, the digits-only `TEXT(…,"0")` locale-proofing, IFERROR→empty-string rather than an error token) exists only in code. ALL 3 B-runs reconstructed it as a requirement of equal weight to the Price formula (B1 SHEET-TICK-005, B2 005, B3 006); ZERO A-runs produced anything resembling a second ticker-bearing cell.

ONE-ROW-PER-SYMBOL INVARIANT WITH A TYPED, DISPLAY-PINNED LOUD ERROR. SPEC: silent on row identity, on duplicates, and on any failure mode — SHEET-MAP-001 names no error at all. CODE: `render_positions` (crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs:547-552) carries `let mut seen: BTreeSet<&Symbol>` and returns `Err(ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow(symbol.clone()))` on a repeat; `ViewError`'s `Display` is `write!(f, "{self:?}")` (line 422-426), and tests/mapping.rs:138-139 pins the exact surface: `format!("{err}") == "DuplicateSymbolRow(\"AMZN\")"`. The rationale the code states (symbol is the row-identity key the marks read-back joins on; the guard is structurally unreachable through `Snapshot.positions: Map<Symbol,_>`) is also unstated in the spec. All 3 B-runs reconstructed the clause, its defensive/unreachable character, and the Debug-shaped Display (B1 SHEET-TICK-007, B2 007, B3 009).

EXACT PRICE-FORMULA LITERAL, THE `"price"` ATTRIBUTE, LIVE-CELL TYPING, AND A NEGATIVE RAW-SYMBOL RULE. SPEC: "build the `Price` formula" — no shape, no attribute, no cell-type, no prohibition. CODE: `price_formula(ticker)` (line 262-264) returns `Cell::Formula(format!("=GOOGLEFINANCE(\"{ticker}\",\"price\")"))` — leading `=`, ticker double-quoted, literal `"price"` attribute, US-comma separator. tests/formula.rs:24-65 pins that Price (index 4 / column E) is a `Cell::Formula` and never an engine `Cell::Value`; tests/mapping.rs:54-61 adds a NEGATIVE requirement the spec never states — `assert!(!price.contains("\"BRK\""))`, i.e. the raw pre-resolution symbol must not appear as the quoted argument when an alias exists. All 3 B-runs pinned the literal and the formula-not-value typing (B1 004, B2 004+006, B3 005+007+008). Lower severity than the items above because all 3 A-runs independently guessed the identical shape — the openness is real but the two directions did not diverge on the value.

THE DISPLAYED SYMBOL AND THE ORACLE KEY DIVERGE. CODE: the Positions `Symbol` cell is `Cell::Value(symbol.clone())` — the RAW ledger symbol, un-normalized (crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs:584) — while the same row's Price and Quote Date cells carry the trimmed/upper-cased/aliased ticker; and `read_marks` (line 824-893) keys the settle pass and the produced `MarksProduced.marks` by that same raw `Symbol`. So normalization is scoped to the oracle lookup only and never rewrites what the sheet shows or what the read-back joins on. SPEC: says nothing about a Symbol column, about scoping, or about which form the read-back keys on. B1 states it as its own clause (SHEET-TICK-008); B2/B3 imply it. Practical edge the pairing creates: a Symbol carrying stray whitespace renders as-is in column A while pricing under the normalized ticker.

RESOLUTION IS TOTAL, UNVALIDATED, ONE-HOP — AND THE FAILURE IT DEFERS IS CLASSIFIED DOWNSTREAM. CODE: `resolve_ticker` returns `String`, never `Result`; the alias VALUE is used verbatim and never re-resolved (no chaining, no cycle handling, no exchange inference, no ticker-form validation), and there is no escaping of `"` inside a ticker before it is interpolated into the quoted formula literal. A ticker GOOGLEFINANCE cannot price surfaces only later, as `PriceReading::Permanent` → `DegradeReason::Permanent` (line 299-301, 888-890) — no mark, no prior carry-forward. SPEC: names no failure mode, no validation duty, and no degrade classification. B2 (008) and B3 (010) both reconstructed this as an explicit negative requirement; B3 also pins "never returns empty for a non-empty symbol".

notes:
CLASSIFICATION RATIONALE — BD-DRIFT rather than B-ONLY-DRIFT. The B side alone would already justify B-ONLY-DRIFT (four distinct code-side surpluses), but the normalization gap is genuinely bidirectional: it is not merely that the code pins a rule the spec omits, it is that all three A-runs, working from the spec text alone, implemented the CONTRARY rule and each flagged the sub-decision as forced invention in their assumption lists. Under the stated Direction-A definition ("a sub-decision the spec leaves open, forcing the A-outputs to invent"), that is an A signal landing on the same gap the B side reconstructs — hence BD. The spec's own phrase "(identity when unset)" is the load-bearing text: it reads as raw passthrough, and the code's `" amzn "` → `"AMZN"` is not identity.

ASSUMPTION ARTIFACTS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED FROM FINDINGS (unanimous A-side, no spec basis):
1. Quote-escaping. All three A-runs implement `escape_sheets_string`/`escape` doubling `"` before interpolation, and all three label it invented/defensive (A3 assumption 8: "invented defensively; no injection/escaping requirement appears in the EARS"). The real `price_formula` does no escaping. Because SHEET-MAP-001 says nothing about escaping, this is an artifact, not drift — though it is worth noting to the arrow owner that a ticker containing `"` would emit a malformed formula, and nothing in spec or code prevents one.
2. Types and shape of the config seam. All three A-runs invented a sheets-view-local `SheetsConfig { ticker_aliases: BTreeMap<..> }`; the real seam is `config::AliasMap` with a `resolve(&str) -> String` method (crates/config/src/lib.rs:277-300). The spec's "`config`'s alias map" underdetermines this, but no behavior diverges.
3. `Ticker`/`PriceFormula` newtypes vs the code's plain `String` + `Cell::Formula`. Presentation only.

AMBIGUITY BOTH SIDES NOTICED AND RESOLVED THE SAME WAY: "unset" — whole-map-absent vs per-symbol-miss. A1 and A2 both explicitly flagged the ambiguity and chose per-symbol miss; the code (`AliasMap::resolve`'s `get(...).unwrap_or_else(identity)`) agrees. No drift, but the spec sentence would read better with the per-key reading made explicit.

STABILITY DETAIL. A-side high: three near-identical implementations — same alias-then-identity resolution, same `=GOOGLEFINANCE("<t>","price")` literal with explicit `"price"` attribute, same exact/case-sensitive lookup, same infallible signature, same quote-doubling, same "no chaining" and "no validation" assumptions. Divergence is cosmetic only (struct naming, `String` vs newtype return, `BTreeMap<String,String>` vs `BTreeMap<Symbol,Ticker>`). B-side high: all three reconstructed the same eight-to-ten clauses in the same order of importance — normalization, verbatim alias value, normalized identity fallback, the Price literal, the Quote Date companion with every constant (`tradetime`, `DATE(1970,1,1)`, `TEXT(…,"0")`, `IFERROR`→empty), the negative raw-symbol rule, and `DuplicateSymbolRow` with its Debug-shaped Display. They differ only in ID prefix (SHEET-TICK-* vs SHEET-MAP-*) and granularity (8 vs 8 vs 10 clauses); B3 additionally names the `resolve_ticker(aliases, symbol)` signature and the `Cell::Formula` typing as its own clause.

SCOPE CAVEAT FOR THE ARROW OWNER: findings 2, 3, 5 and 6 describe behavior that may legitimately belong to sibling specs (SHEET-MARK-*, a Positions-render spec). This audit judges only against the SHEET-MAP-001 text supplied. The point that survives regardless of where the clauses land is that the resolved ticker — SHEET-MAP-001's own output — feeds a second GOOGLEFINANCE formula whose existence SHEET-MAP-001 does not admit, so a reader of this spec alone cannot know that changing resolution changes two cells, not one.
